subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron runs get an explicit `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep only per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This defines a scheduled-run tool-execution boundary and new public config semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent security and compatibility contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add cron-specific policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron sessions as covered by `tools.subagents.tools`, reducing config surface but coupling cron and subagent semantics.

options.title: Keep current safeguards
options.body: Leave cron control to per-job `toolsAllow` and announce delivery safeguards, accepting that there is no global cron deny boundary.

recommendation.title: Add cron-specific policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest prior-review and recent cron/tool-policy history for choosing this security boundary.
